name: Quarks
kicker: Subatomic building blocks · Bound by the strong force into protons
briefing: Quarks are tiny particles that combine in twos or threes to build protons, neutrons, and every other particle felt by the strong force. Physicists Murray Gell-Mann and George Zweig proposed them in 1964, and Gell-Mann borrowed their odd name from a nonsense word in James Joyce’s _Finnegans Wake_. They come in six “flavors” with names like up, down, charm, and strange, and the strong force confines them so tightly that no one has ever isolated a single one.

tossups.p: The “Eightfold Way,” developed by Murray Gell-Mann and Yuval Ne’eman, classified particles in a scheme that led to the proposal of these particles, which deep inelastic scattering experiments later confirmed. The CKM matrix describes how these particles “mix” through interactions with the weak force.
tossups.r: Murray Gell-Mann and George Zweig proposed the existence of these particles in 1964. For 10 points, name these elementary particles that combine to form protons and neutrons.

tossups.p: A 1974 discovery nicknamed the “November Revolution,” made independently by Burton Richter and Samuel Ting, confirmed a new, heavier type of one of these particles called “charm.” These particles are governed by a theory called quantum chromodynamics, which assigns them a property called color charge.
tossups.r: Three of these particles bind together through the strong force to form a baryon, while one of these particles paired with an antiparticle forms a meson. For 10 points, name these particles that come in six flavors, including up and down.

tossups.p: These particles are theorized to have briefly formed a free-roaming plasma with gluons in the first several microseconds after the Big Bang, before cooling enough to lock into protons and neutrons. Unlike most forces, the strong force binding these particles actually gets weaker at very short distances, a property called asymptotic freedom.
tossups.r: These particles cannot be observed individually, a restriction called color confinement. For 10 points, name these particles that make up protons and neutrons.

tossups.p: Murray Gell-Mann borrowed the everyday name for these particles from a nonsense word in James Joyce’s novel _Finnegans Wake_. The heaviest type of these particles, nicknamed “top,” was not confirmed until 1995 at Fermilab.
tossups.r: These particles carry a fractional electric charge of either positive two-thirds or negative one-third. For 10 points, name these particles, which come in six flavors and combine in threes to form protons and neutrons.

tossups.p: In 2015, physicists at the Large Hadron Collider announced evidence for an exotic bound state made of five of these particles. These particles are the only known elementary particles said to interact through all four fundamental forces, including gravity.
tossups.r: Emitting a W boson can change one of these particles from one flavor into another. For 10 points, name these elementary particles that combine to form protons and neutrons.

tossups.p: These particles cannot exist in isolation, a restriction called color confinement, and the force between them actually weakens at short distances, a property called asymptotic freedom. The CKM matrix describes how these particles mix through the weak force.

These particles are believed to have briefly existed as a free-roaming plasma with gluons within the first several microseconds after the Big Bang.

trap.title: Quarks, or electrons?
trap.body: Both are fundamental particles smaller than an atom, but they belong to different families. Electrons are leptons and are never affected by the strong force, so they never combine to form protons, neutrons, or any other particle built from the strong force. These particles, by contrast, are held together by the strong force (carried by gluons) and combine in threes to build every proton and neutron.
trap.fix: If the clues mention the strong force, gluons, color charge, confinement, protons, or neutrons, they want this answer. If the clues mention orbiting the nucleus, electric current, or the lightest charged particle, they want electrons instead.
